## Fixture and live boundary

Live (real code, real Postgres test database, factories for rows, no mocks on the request path): the Ritual admin add page and its POST (a staff superuser through the Django test client), the reswear options endpoint, the ritual perform endpoint and the Rite of Re-swearing service, the vow picks catalog, the telnet command handler running vow reswear and vow picks, the combat encounter check (a real encounter and participant row), the action point pool, anima and the consumed Token of the Vow. Every payload under payloads/ was recorded from that stack at 615c8ef805c71a5722ecee6b6af01956674c9219 (the reviewed_commit field inside each file says so); the reviewed revision 52d6f06b5e916424da3bb1bcfc03ef0c252e85c0 differs from it only in frontend/src/character_sheets/sheet.css, a CSS-only change that no endpoint, action or command reads, so the payloads are unaffected and were not re-recorded. Rows were authored with factories to mirror the demo's Quicksilver example (names, prices, limits, a budget of 4 per level) and are example data, not the production catalog. The rite itself was not made by a factory: it was created by the admin POST recorded in payloads/01-admin-creates-the-rite.json.

Replayed (fixture boundary): the browser pages, every screenshot of which was re-shot at the reviewed revision. No game server was started (shared devcontainer rule). The real, unmodified frontend at this revision was served by Vite and every request to /api/ was answered by Playwright route interception from the recorded real payloads (payloads/02, 03, 07, 08, 09 and the roster, user and sheet reads in payloads/20-browser-reads.json); the list of requests the pages made is payloads/browser-requests.json. Requests the sheet makes for unrelated panels were answered with an empty list, so those blocks read as empty. The Change picks, row and Perform the rite clicks are real; the answer to Perform is the recorded real answer (success, or the recorded real 400 for a fight or short action points), and the catalog re-read after success is the recorded real catalog after the swap. The Ritual admin page itself was not rendered in the browser; its select options, its refusal of an unlisted path and the created row are the recorded payload.

## Tested interactions

All through real interfaces. Expected values come from the issue spec, the covenants rules (a pick's price is max(1, floor(value x product of limit frequencies) - reductions); a level's chosen picks may cost no more than the budget) and the maintainer rulings, not from the code's own output.

1. Staff create the rite in the Ritual admin by choosing its service: [payloads/01-admin-creates-the-rite.json](payloads/01-admin-creates-the-rite.json). Expected: a select (not free text) listing the registered services with Covenants: Rite of Re-swearing among them; an unlisted path refused; choosing the rite's path creates a SERVICE ritual; the Required content probe goes from missing to present. Saw: the select lists 24 services, the first Covenants: Rite of Re-swearing; posting os.system returned the add page again with "Select a valid choice. os.system is not one of the available choices." and no row; posting the rite's path with 10 anima and one component (Token of the Vow) returned 302 to the changelist and created row 6, execution_kind SERVICE, the reswear service path; the probe went from missing "the Rite of Re-swearing" to present.
2. The reswear options endpoint for a chosen-pick holder: [payloads/03-reswear-options.json](payloads/03-reswear-options.json). Saw ritual_id 6, ap_cost 3, anima_cost 10, components ["Token of the Vow"], component_ids [6] (her carried token), no unavailable reason. Another account reading it gets 404 ([payloads/04-reswear-options-other-account.json](payloads/04-reswear-options-other-account.json)); the catalog before the swap is [payloads/02-catalog-before.json](payloads/02-catalog-before.json) and the options after it (component_ids empty because the token was spent) are [payloads/09-reswear-options-after.json](payloads/09-reswear-options-after.json); it still answers 200 in a fight ([payloads/05-fight-refusal-options-still-read.json](payloads/05-fight-refusal-options-still-read.json)).
3. Successful re-swear through the web perform path: [payloads/07-web-reswear-success.json](payloads/07-web-reswear-success.json). Ysmay held level 1 Strike from the Flank and Quick Recovery (4 of 4) and level 2 Bleeding Cut, with 10 action points, 20 anima and one Token of the Vow. POST /api/magic/rituals/perform/ giving up Quick Recovery for Feint and Vanish, with the options' component ids. Expected: the old pick gone, the new one chosen, 3 AP and 10 anima and the token spent. Saw 200, "You perform Rite of Re-swearing. You give up Quick Recovery and take Feint and Vanish. Level 1: 4 of 4. 3 AP spent."; action points 10 to 7, anima 20 to 10, tokens held 1 to 0, chosen picks Bleeding Cut, Quick Recovery, Strike from the Flank becoming Bleeding Cut, Feint and Vanish, Strike from the Flank. The catalog after ([payloads/08-catalog-after.json](payloads/08-catalog-after.json)) shows Feint and Vanish chosen and Quick Recovery open again but over what is left; repeating the same request is refused with "You have not chosen that pick." and spends nothing ([payloads/10-web-repeat-after-success.json](payloads/10-web-repeat-after-success.json)).
4. Seven web refusals, each with action points, anima, tokens and chosen picks read before and after: [payloads/06-web-refusals.json](payloads/06-web-refusals.json). All 400 (the last a 400 on the serializer) and every state identical before and after: a different level ("Read the Feint is a level 2 pick and Quick Recovery is level 1; a pick changes only for one of the same level."), over budget ("Light on Your Feet costs 4; giving up Quick Recovery leaves 2 of the 4 points for level 1 picks."), a pick not chosen ("You have not chosen that pick."), a pick already held ("You have already chosen Strike from the Flank."), short of action points with 2 held ("The rite takes 3 action points, and you have 2."), in an encounter ("You cannot re-swear a vow pick during a fight."), and another account performing as her sheet ("character_sheet_id does not belong to the requesting account.").
5. Telnet: [payloads/30-telnet-transcripts.json](payloads/30-telnet-transcripts.json). vow reswear quick recovery=Feint and Vanish printed the same success line as the web, action points 10 to 7, anima 20 to 10, token 1 to 0, and vow picks afterwards shows Feint and Vanish chosen and Quick Recovery "costs more than is left". Refusals with nothing spent: a different level, over budget, "You have not chosen a pick named Light on Your Feet.", the usage line for vow reswear Quick Recovery, short of action points, and in an encounter. A further swap back with the token gone printed "Ritual 'Rite of Re-swearing' requires 1x 'Token of the Vow' but only 0 provided." and spent nothing.
6. Browser, sheet Ties section as the owner: the panel shows a Change picks button under the "Chosen picks change only through the Rite of Re-swearing." line (four shots). Clicking it opens the dialog with the demo's swap preselected (Quick Recovery for Feint and Vanish), the ledger reading "4 of 4 · Quick Recovery, Strike from the Flank" before and "4 of 4 · Feint and Vanish, Strike from the Flank" after, and the cost "3 AP from this week · 10 anima · Token of the Vow" ([payloads/browser-notes.json](payloads/browser-notes.json)). Light on Your Feet is dimmed with "costs more than is left" and cannot be chosen (the force click left the selection unchanged). Choosing Bleeding Cut then Through the Gap at level 2 shows "3 of 4" before and "4 of 4 · Through the Gap" after. Perform the rite sent ritual_id 6, old_pick_id 40, new_pick_id 41, covenant_id 6, components [6], closed the dialog, re-read the catalog and showed the success line under the panel in all four combinations. Two recorded refusals show in the dialog's alert line.

## Comparison notes

Screen 9. The build reproduces every drawn element, in the demo's order: the title and pick-level tag, Give up and Take instead, the before and after ledger lines, the cost line, the fight note and the perform button, in dark, light, desktop and phone. Differences judged not to be defects, with reasons:
- Give up lists every chosen pick (Quick Recovery, Strike from the Flank, Bleeding Cut), each with its price, where the demo draws one example row. The demo puts one Change picks control on the panel (screen 8) rather than one per pick, so the player must choose which pick to give up somewhere; the spec scope says the panel lists the same level's other picks and whether each fits. Choosing a pick of another level rebuilds Take instead for that level (level 2 shots).
- Take instead shows Light on Your Feet dimmed with "costs more than is left"; the demo draws one fitting pick. The reason text is the one screen 8 uses for a pick over budget.
- The ledger lists picks alphabetically (server order), where the demo lists Strike from the Flank first; the demo's own order is example text.
- Fonts and button colour follow the app's sheet tokens, not the demo's monospace values and brown button; the demo's own caption says every name, number and description is an example.
- The dialog is a modal over the sheet with a close control; the demo draws the panel standalone.
- On desktop the Change picks button sits under the note, not right-aligned beside it, because the panel lives in the sheet's 352 px right rail; the demo draws it full width. At phone width the demo stacks them the same way. This is the same responsive wrap accepted for the header tag in slice 6.
- The success line "You perform Rite of Re-swearing. You give up Quick Recovery and take Feint and Vanish. Level 1: 4 of 4. 3 AP spent." shows under the panel; the demo draws no result state.

Screen 10 (telnet) draws no reswear line, so nothing is compared; the verb was checked anyway and its output is in payloads/30-telnet-transcripts.json. The vow picks lines are unchanged from slice 6.

Unbuilt demo affordances: none. The demo's "today" and "in spec" notes list the rite's AP cost and its refusal in a fight, both built.

F1 (first pass defect, closed): the dialog's refusal line reuses .vowpicks-error, whose colour was hsl(var(--destructive)): rgb(127,29,29) on the dialog's rgb(9,9,11) in dark, 1.99 to 1. The reviewed revision adds `.dark .vowpicks-error { color: hsl(0 72% 65%); }` (frontend/src/character_sheets/sheet.css); re-shot and re-measured in the browser: rgb(230,101,101), 6.08 to 1, for both refusals, desktop and phone (reswear-dialog-refused-fight-dark-desktop.png, reswear-dialog-refused-ap-dark-desktop.png, reswear-dialog-refused-fight-dark-phone.png). The same class draws the slice 6 panel's Choose refusal, which is lifted too.

F2 (first pass defect, closed): the shared dialog shell's close button overlapped the header tag. The reviewed revision adds `padding-right: 2rem` to .vowpicks-rite-head; measured in the browser after the dialog settled, the tag's right edge is 24 px short of the close button at desktop (919 against 943) and at phone (333 against 357), and the 3x zoom shows the glyphs apart (header-clearance-light-desktop.png, header-clearance-dark-phone.png). The tag stays right-aligned in every state (reswear-dialog-open shots).

Residual, not a demo divergence and not blocking: in the light theme the refusal line is still rgb(239,68,68) on white, 3.76 to 1, which passes the 3 to 1 bar for large text but not 4.5 to 1 for body text. It is the sheet-wide destructive token that other sheet rules (sheet.css lines 546, 582 and 1015) use unchanged, and the maintainer's fix scoped the lift to the dark sheet. Reported so the call is visible; it is the one place the first-pass F1 numbers were not fully changed.

Mechanical companion proposal: a vitest that renders the real ReswearDialog with a failed perform and asserts that every class it emits (vowpicks-rite, vowpicks-rite-head, vowpicks-two, vowpicks-swap, vowpicks-ledger, vowpicks-rite-foot, vowpicks-error) has a rule in sheet.css, plus a contrast check that the .vowpicks-error colour token resolves to at least 4.5 to 1 against the dialog background in both themes. No class here lacks a rule: all are styled in the screenshots, and the page imports sheet.css itself.

Observed and not a defect: in the after-success shots the Change picks button looks filled because the pointer was resting on it (hover state).

## Unresolved findings

None
